readings.en: Wisdom breathes life into her sons
readings.plain: breathes life into her sons

why: The Plain follows the Greek. The Hebrew uses the plural form chokhmot for Wisdom, as Proverbs 9:1 does.

a: The one who listens to her will judge nations
p: The Hebrew has Wisdom speak: "Whoever listens to me will judge truth."

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete; the base text of this site
readings.orig: ὁ ὑπακούων αὐτῆς κρινεῖ ἔθνη
readings.en: the one who obeys her will judge nations
readings.plain: The one who listens to her will judge nations

readings.w: Hebrew, Cairo Genizah manuscript A (a medieval copy; Cambridge University Library, T-S 12.863–864), as transcribed by Martin Abegg
readings.orig: שומע לי ישפט אמת
readings.en: the one who listens to me will judge truth
readings.plain: The one who listens to me will judge with truth

why: The Plain follows the Greek. The Hebrew word for "truth" ('emet, אמת) is very close in writing to a Hebrew word for "nations" ('ummot, אמות); the grandson may have read it that way. This is Claude's suggestion from the letters; the Hebrew manuscript is the medieval copy, so its own reading could also be a change.

a: If you put your trust in her, you will receive her as your inheritance
p: Vaticanus has "you" in the first half and "his" in the second; other codices have "he" throughout.

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete; the base text of this site as first written
readings.orig: ἐὰν ἐμπιστεύσῃς, κατακληρονομήσεις αὐτήν
readings.en: if you trust, you will inherit her
readings.plain: If you put your trust in her, you will receive her as your inheritance

readings.w: A corrector of Vaticanus, Codex Sinaiticus (ℵ), Codex Alexandrinus (A) and Codex Ephraemi (C), in Swete's notes; the KJV ("If a man commit himself unto her")
readings.orig: ἐὰν ἐμπιστεύσῃ, κατακληρονομήσει αὐτήν
readings.en: if he trusts, he will inherit her
readings.plain: If he puts his trust in her, he will receive her as his inheritance

why: The Plain follows Swete's text, though the other reading fits "his descendants" in the second line better.

a: At the start she will go with him by crooked ways.
t: The Hebrew: "I walk with him in disguise"
p: In the Hebrew Wisdom speaks: "For I walk with him in disguise, and at first she tests him with trials."

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete; the base text of this site
readings.orig: ὅτι διεστραμμένως πορεύεται μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ ἐν πρώτοις
readings.en: for she goes with him crookedly at first
readings.plain: At the start she will go with him by crooked ways.

readings.w: Hebrew, Cairo Genizah manuscript A (a medieval copy; Cambridge University Library, T-S 12.863–864), as transcribed by Martin Abegg
readings.orig: כי בהתנכר אלך עמו ולפנים יבחרנו בנסיונות
readings.en: For in disguise I walk with him, and at first she tests him with trials
readings.plain: For I walk with him in disguise, / and at first I test him with trials.

why: The Plain follows the Greek. The Hebrew verb hitnakker means "make oneself a stranger, disguise oneself": Wisdom hides who she is from the beginner. The Greek "crookedly" may be the grandson's way of saying the same.

a: Do not hold back a word at a time when it could bring rescue.
t: A second line: "Do not hide your wisdom"
p: Vaticanus has one line; the Hebrew and the Latin add "do not hide your wisdom," which the KJV has.

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete; the base text of this site
readings.orig: μὴ κωλύσῃς λόγον ἐν καιρῷ σωτηρίας
readings.en: do not hold back a word at a time of salvation
readings.plain: Do not hold back a word at a time when it could bring rescue.

readings.w: Hebrew, Cairo Genizah manuscript A (a medieval copy; Cambridge University Library, T-S 12.863–864), as transcribed by Martin Abegg
readings.orig: אל תמנע דבר בעולם אל תצפין את חכמתך
readings.en: Do not hold back a word [be'olam]; do not hide your wisdom
readings.plain: Do not hold back a word when it is needed; / do not hide your wisdom.

readings.w: The Latin Vulgate (4:28), followed by the KJV ("and hide not thy wisdom in her beauty")
readings.orig: nec retineas verbum in tempore salutis. Non abscondas sapientiam tuam in decore suo
readings.en: do not hold back a word in the time of salvation; do not hide your wisdom in its beauty
readings.plain: Do not hold back a word at a time when it could bring rescue, / and do not hide your wisdom in its beauty.

why: The Plain follows the base text. The Hebrew shows that the second line is old. Its first line has be'olam, usually "forever" or "in the world," which is hard here; the English given is only approximate.

a: confessing your sins
p: The Greek says "do not be ashamed to confess your sins"; the Hebrew, "do not be ashamed to turn back from sin."

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete; the base text of this site
readings.orig: μὴ αἰσχυνθῇς ὁμολογῆσαι ἐφ᾽ ἁμαρτίαις σου
readings.en: do not be ashamed to confess your sins
readings.plain: confessing your sins

readings.w: Hebrew, Cairo Genizah manuscript A (a medieval copy; Cambridge University Library, T-S 12.863–864), as transcribed by Martin Abegg
readings.orig: אל תבוש לשוב מעון ואל תעמוד לפני שבלת
readings.en: Do not be ashamed to turn from iniquity, and do not stand before a flood
readings.plain: turning away from sin

readings.w: The Latin Vulgate (4:31)
readings.orig: Non confundaris confiteri peccata tua, et ne subjicias te omni homini pro peccato
readings.en: do not be ashamed to confess your sins, and do not submit yourself to every man for sin
readings.plain: confessing your sins, / and do not put yourself under every man because of sin

why: The Plain follows the Greek. The Hebrew's "turn" (shuv) is repentance; the Greek's "confess" is saying it aloud. The two belong together (Proverbs 28:13, "the one who admits them and turns from them will receive mercy").

a: and do not favor the face of a powerful man
t: An extra line in the Hebrew
p: The Hebrew adds "Do not sit with an unjust judge, for you will have to judge as he pleases."

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete; the base text of this site

readings.plain: and do not favor the face of a powerful man

readings.orig: ואל תמאן לפני מושלים אל תשב עם שופט עול כי כאשר כרצונו תשפט עמו
readings.en: and do not refuse before rulers; do not sit with an unjust judge, for you will judge with him as he wishes
readings.plain: and do not refuse in front of rulers. / Do not sit with an unjust judge, / for you will have to judge the way he wants.

why: The Plain follows the Greek. The extra Hebrew lines are not in the Greek or the Latin. The online edition's index of the manuscript lists the line about the unjust judge as 8:14, where the Greek has a similar warning about going to law with a judge.

a: for what is true
p: The Greek and the Hebrew differ in the word: the Greek has "the truth," the Hebrew "righteousness."

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete; the base text of this site

readings.orig: pro justitia
readings.en: for justice
readings.plain: for what is just

why: The Plain follows the Greek. Ben Sira's Hebrew tsedeq is righteousness or justice, which the Latin keeps.

a: Do not be rough when you speak
p: Vaticanus has "rough"; Sinaiticus as first written and Alexandrinus have "quick," which the KJV follows.

readings.plain: Do not be hasty when you speak

readings.orig: μὴ γίνου θρασὺς ἐν γλώσσῃ σου
readings.en: do not be bold in your tongue
readings.plain: Do not be brash when you speak

why: The Greek words differ by one letter. The Plain follows the base text; the Hebrew of manuscript A has a word that may mean "arrogant" (gavhan).

a: do not act like a lion
p: The Greek has "like a lion"; the Hebrew has "like a dog."

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete; the base text of this site
readings.orig: μὴ ἴσθι ὡς λέων ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ σου

readings.plain: do not act like a lion

readings.orig: אל תהי ככלב בביתך
readings.en: do not be like a dog in your house
readings.plain: do not act like a dog

why: The Plain follows the Greek. A dog snaps and growls; a lion terrifies. Either way the master is not to bully his household.

a: and do not say, "It is enough for me."
t: "It is enough" or "It is in my power"
p: The Hebrew reads "and do not say, 'It is in the power of my hand.'"

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete; the base text of this site
readings.orig: καὶ μὴ εἴπῃς Αὐτάρκη μοί ἐστιν

readings.plain: and do not say, "It is enough for me."

readings.orig: ואל תאמר יש לאל ידי
readings.en: and do not say, "It is in the power of my hand"
readings.plain: and do not say, "I have the power to do it."

why: The Plain follows the Greek. The Hebrew idiom is the one Laban uses in Genesis 31:29 ("It is in my power to do you harm").

a: The Lord is an avenger, and he will make you pay.
t: "The Lord will avenge" or "God seeks the pursued"
p: The Hebrew reads "for the LORD seeks out the pursued," words found in Ecclesiastes 3:15.

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete; the base text of this site
readings.orig: ὁ γὰρ κύριος ἐκδικῶν ἐκδικήσει σε
readings.en: for the Lord, avenging, will avenge you
readings.plain: The Lord is an avenger, and he will make you pay.

readings.w: Hebrew, Cairo Genizah manuscript A (a medieval copy; Cambridge University Library, T-S 12.863–864), as transcribed by Martin Abegg (the divine name written as three yods)
readings.orig: כי ייי מבקש נרדפים
readings.en: for the LORD seeks the pursued
readings.plain: For the LORD seeks out the ones pursued.

why: The Plain follows the Greek. In the Hebrew, God takes the side of those the proud man oppresses; compare Ecclesiastes 3:15, "God seeks out what is pursued."

a: and give your reply with patience
t: An extra line in the KJV
p: The KJV has "and let thy life be sincere" in the middle of the verse.

readings.orig: (no Greek given here)
readings.en: and let thy life be sincere; and with patience give answer
readings.plain: and let your life be sincere, / and give your reply with patience

why: The extra line is not in the codices Swete prints. The Plain follows the base text.

a: do not get trapped by your own tongue
t: "Be trapped by" or "lie in wait with" the tongue
p: Vaticanus as first written has "do not be trapped"; its corrector and the other codices, "do not lie in wait," as the KJV has.

readings.plain: do not get trapped by your own tongue

readings.w: A corrector of Vaticanus, Codex Sinaiticus (ℵ), Codex Alexandrinus (A) and Codex Ephraemi (C), in Swete's notes; the KJV ("lie not in wait with thy tongue")
readings.orig: τῇ γλώσσῃ σου μὴ ἐνέδρευε
readings.en: do not lie in wait with your tongue
readings.plain: do not set ambushes with your tongue

why: The Plain follows Swete's text. Most codices make the speaker the one who sets the trap; Vaticanus makes him its victim.

a: do not act in ignorance,
t: "Do not be ignorant" or "do not ruin"
p: The Greek says "do not be ignorant"; the Hebrew, "do not ruin anything, small or great."

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete; the base text of this site

readings.orig: מעט והרבה אל תשחת
readings.en: little and much, do not ruin
readings.plain: do nothing to ruin anyone,

readings.w: The Latin Vulgate (5:18)
readings.orig: Justifica pusillum et magnum similiter
readings.en: Do justice to the small and the great alike
readings.plain: give the small and the great the same justice,

why: The Plain follows the Greek. The three witnesses agree only on "small and great."

a: Do not puff yourself up in your soul's schemes
t: The Hebrew: "the hand of your appetite"
p: The Hebrew reads "Do not fall into the hand of your appetite."

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete; the base text of this site
readings.orig: μὴ ἐπάρῃς σεαυτὸν ἐν βουλῇ ψυχῆς σου
readings.en: do not exalt yourself in the counsel of your soul
readings.plain: Do not puff yourself up in your soul's schemes

readings.orig: אל תפול ביד נפשך
readings.en: do not fall into the hand of your appetite
readings.plain: Do not fall into the grip of your own appetite

why: The Plain follows the Greek. The Hebrew makes the danger plain: desire that takes over. Its second line is hard to read.

a: a medicine that gives life
p: The Hebrew calls a faithful friend "a bundle of life," as in 1 Samuel 25:29; the Latin adds "and immortality."

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete; the base text of this site
readings.orig: φάρμακον ζωῆς
readings.en: a medicine of life
readings.plain: a medicine that gives life

readings.w: Hebrew, Cairo Genizah manuscript A (a medieval copy; Cambridge University Library, T-S 12.863–864), as transcribed by Martin Abegg
readings.orig: צרור חיים אוהב אמונה
readings.en: a bundle of life is a faithful friend
readings.plain: a bundle that keeps life safe

readings.w: The Latin Vulgate (6:16), followed by the Douay-Rheims
readings.orig: medicamentum vitae et immortalitatis
readings.en: the medicine of life and immortality
readings.plain: a medicine of life and immortality

why: The Plain follows the Greek. The Hebrew tsror chayyim is Abigail's phrase: "my lord's life will be tied up safe in the bundle of the living" (1 Samuel 25:29). The Greek may have read tsori, "balm, medicine," for tseror, "bundle"; the two words share their first letters (Claude's suggestion).

a: How rough she is for the untaught!
p: Vaticanus as first written has "swift"; its corrector, Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus have "rough," which the Plain follows.

readings.w: A corrector of Vaticanus, Codex Sinaiticus (ℵ) and Codex Alexandrinus (A), in Swete's notes; the KJV ("very unpleasant"); the Latin (Vulgate 6:21, aspera)
readings.orig: ὡς τραχεῖά ἐστιν σφόδρα τοῖς ἀπαιδεύτοις
readings.en: how very rough she is to the uninstructed
readings.plain: How rough she is for the untaught!

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete; the base text of this site as first written
readings.orig: ὡς ταχεῖά ἐστιν σφόδρα τοῖς ἀπαιδεύτοις
readings.en: how very swift she is to the uninstructed
readings.plain: How swift she is for the untaught!

readings.w: Hebrew, Cairo Genizah manuscript A (a medieval copy; Cambridge University Library, T-S 12.863–864), as transcribed by Martin Abegg; also the Qumran fragment 2Q18 (DJD III)
readings.orig: עקובה היא לאויל
readings.en: she is rugged for the stubborn fool
readings.plain: How rugged she is for the stubborn fool!

why: Here the Plain departs from Swete's text. "Swift" makes no sense with what follows, the Hebrew of both manuscripts has "rugged," and the other codices and a corrector of Vaticanus have "rough." The two Greek words differ by one letter.

a: Wisdom lives up to her name
p: The Hebrew says "discipline (musar) is like its name," a pun; the Greek put "wisdom."

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete; the base text of this site
readings.orig: σοφία γὰρ κατὰ τὸ ὄνομα αὐτῆς ἐστιν
readings.en: for wisdom is according to her name
readings.plain: Wisdom lives up to her name

readings.w: Hebrew, Cairo Genizah manuscript A (a medieval copy; Cambridge University Library, T-S 12.863–864), as transcribed by Martin Abegg; also the Qumran fragment 2Q18 (DJD III)
readings.orig: כי המוסר כשמה כן הוא ולא לרבים היא נכחה
readings.en: for discipline is like its name, so it is, and it is not plain to many
readings.plain: Discipline lives up to its name

why: The Plain follows the Greek. The pun is in the Hebrew: musar, "discipline," is spelled like the word for "turned aside, withdrawn" (from sur, "turn aside"), so discipline "is as her name": kept back, and not plain to many. The grandson could not carry the pun into Greek and wrote "wisdom" (Claude's reading of the wordplay).

a: and her collar a robe of glory
p: Vaticanus reads "her branches"; Alexandrinus and Ephraemi have "her collars," the word of 6:24, which the Plain follows.

readings.orig: καὶ οἱ κλάδοι αὐτῆς εἰς στολὴν δόξης
readings.en: and her branches into a robe of glory
readings.plain: and her branches a robe of glory

readings.orig: וחבלתה בגדי כתם

why: Here the Plain departs from Swete's text. The verse answers 6:24, where the same Greek has her "collar" (klois); "branches" (kladoi) looks like a copying slip between two similar words.

a: He will steady your heart
p: The Hebrew reads "he will give your heart understanding, and what you desire, he will make you wise."
